newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arthuis says France supported weaker lira.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says France supported weaker lira.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday France had suppported a weaker central rate for the lira than that finally agreed by EU finance ministers for the Italian currency's re-entry to the ERM.
He said France had considered a rate of 298 lira per franc would be a fair rate for the lira's central rate in the European Exchange Rate Mechanism. The rate agreed on Sunday was 295 lira per franc.
The first corresponded to 1000 lira per mark, while the second figure, the one finally agreed, corresponded to 990 lira per mark.
His comments were the first indication that France may have supported Italy's drive to bring the lira into the ERM at a central rate of at least 1,000 per mark.
French officials have in the past complained about what they called the "competitive devaluation" when the lira left the ERM in 1992 and fell sharply.
Arthuis told reporters EU finance ministers had to find a rate which was "fair, sustainable and lasting". "We chose this rate because we thought it was fair, sustainable and lasting," he said.

"France played a good role as a mediator," he told reporters, saying there was no substantial difference between its proposed rate and that finally agreed on Sunday. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
